pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: What's the difference between the terminal and the shell? Which one actually ran the commands in the exercise?
expected_points: the terminal is the window/program that draws text and forwards keystrokes
the shell (zsh/bash) reads the command line, runs it, and prints results — it did the work
they are separate programs; the terminal hosts the shell

questions.prompt: You're standing in /Users/ada. Give one absolute and one relative path to the file /Users/ada/trip/notes/draft.txt, and explain what `cd ..` would do from there.
expected_points: absolute paths start at the root /, valid from anywhere
relative paths (e.g. trip/notes/draft.txt) are resolved against the working directory
.. names the parent directory, so cd .. moves up to /Users
pwd tells you what relative paths currently mean

questions.prompt: In the exercise you moved the photos but copied the draft backup. What's the difference between mv and cp — and after rm, can you get a file back?
expected_points: cp duplicates: the original stays where it was
mv relocates (or renames): the original location ends up empty
rm deletes permanently — no Trash, no undo
rmdir only removes empty directories, which is a safety net

questions.prompt: You type a command and the shell says 'command not found'. What is the shell actually telling you, and what's your diagnosis checklist?
expected_points: the shell searched the directories listed in PATH and no executable with that name matched
checklist: typo in the name; program not installed; installed somewhere PATH doesn't list
echo $PATH shows the search list; which <cmd> shows what a command resolves to

questions.prompt: You need ls to show hidden entries but forgot the flag. How do you find out without the internet — and how do you get back out of what opens?
expected_points: man ls opens the manual page; /word searches, q quits
many commands also print usage with --help
look flags up instead of guessing; the local man page matches your system

questions.prompt: A flag from a Linux tutorial errors on macOS. Why can the 'same' command differ between machines, and which documentation wins?
expected_points: macOS ships BSD versions of the core tools, Linux ships GNU versions — flags differ
the man page on your own machine describes the version you actually run

questions.prompt: In `pwd > location.txt`, what does the `>` do, and what's the danger when the file already exists?
expected_points: > redirects the command's output into a file instead of the screen
it creates the file if missing and overwrites (truncates) it if present, without asking
